subject: chemistry
title: Entropy Expanse: Disorder and Direction
welcome_lead: Quantify disorder with ΔS and predict spontaneous change.
meta_desc: A-Level chemistry adventure on entropy and the second law of thermodynamics.
final_note: You have grasped the universal drive towards disorder.

concepts.def: Number of ways particles can be arranged.

walkthroughs.body_html:
ΔS > 0 when: gases form, mol number increases, solid dissolves, temperature rises.

Example: CaCO3(s) -> CaO(s) + CO2(g) has positive ΔS because a gas appears from a solid.

ΔS_surr = -ΔH / T. Units: convert ΔH from kJ to J before dividing by T in K.

Exothermic reactions warm surroundings, raising their entropy (ΔS_surr positive). At low T, |ΔS_surr| is larger.

A change is spontaneous when ΔS_total > 0. This is equivalent to ΔG < 0 at constant T and p.

Endothermic dissolving (NH4NO3 in H2O) is spontaneous because ΔS_system is highly positive enough to outweigh negative ΔS_surr.

mcqs.q: What does an increase in entropy of a system correspond to?
options: Entropy measures how much energy a system contains in total.
Entropy is just a measure of how messy a system looks visually.
An increase in the number of ways energy and particles can be arranged — typically a more dispersed/'disordered' state.
The entropy of the surroundings must stay constant for the process to be spontaneous.

mcqs.q: Why can an endothermic reaction still be spontaneous?
options: All endothermic reactions are spontaneous at room temperature.
If the entropy increase (TΔS) is large enough to outweigh the positive ΔH, ΔG can still be negative.
Entropy measures how much energy a system contains in total.
Endothermic reactions are never spontaneous because they require energy input.

mcqs.q: For a process to be spontaneous, what must happen to the total entropy of the universe?
options: The entropy of the surroundings must stay constant for the process to be spontaneous.
The entropy of the system must increase for the process to be spontaneous.
Entropy measures how much energy a system contains in total.
It must increase (ΔS_total > 0) — the system's entropy alone can decrease as long as the surroundings' entropy increases more.
